none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F=f+ψ over a convex feasible set Q; both f and ψ are convex on Q, and a minimizer exists.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The objective combines differentiable f with a convex regularizer ψ accessible through exact proximal minimization over Q.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Returns ∇f(x) exactly for feasible queries x∈Q. No correctness is required outside Q; no function-value oracle is supplied.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: For a>0, returns an exact minimizer over Q of ‖u−z‖²/(2a)+⟨v,u−z⟩+ψ(u). Gradient and proximal queries consume the same fixed oracle budget.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: On Q, the derivative H of ∇f exists, is positive, and satisfies ‖H‖≤H0+H1(F(x)−F(xstar)). The controlling gap is the full composite objective gap. Public parameters satisfy H0,H1≥0 and R,Δ,ε>0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space. Public x0∈Q has distance at most R from a hidden minimizer xstar and objective gap at most Δ. Neither the minimizer nor its objective value is supplied.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point x must satisfy F(x)−F(xstar)≤ε for a minimizer xstar∈Q.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must belong to Q.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the ε objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within a fixed total oracle budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The composite feasible problem uses curvature controlled by the full objective gap only on the feasible set, with exact gradient and proximal access in a general Hilbert space. This differs from the standard globally Lipschitz-gradient composite formulation.
